newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA ECONOMIC GROWTH ABOUT 10 PCT IN '97-C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: CHINA ECONOMIC GROWTH ABOUT 10 PCT IN '97-C.BANK.

text.p: China's economic growth for 1997 is expected to be about 10 percent while inflation will be curbed to below 4.0 percent, central bank governor Dai Xianglong told a news conference on Thursday.
He forecast economic growth would remain steady at about 8.0 percent over the next two to three years.
Inflation in the next two to three years would be below 5.0 percent, Dai said.
China's benchmark retail price index rose by 0.6 percent year-on-year for July and officials have forecast inflation would be 3.0-4.0 percent this year. Inflation in 1996 was 6.1 percent.
Economic growth in the first half was 9.5 percent, compared with 9.8 percent for all of 1996.

"While pursuing the moderately tight monetary policy, the central bank will make appropriate fine tunings of macro control, improve financial service and facilitate the sustained, rapid and healthy development of the national economy," Dai said.
